positive.query: Build salary bands for our engineering levels L1 to L5 from the survey data I have, targeting the 50th percentile.
Calculate compa-ratios for everyone against our pay ranges and tell me who is below minimum and what it costs to fix.
What range spread and midpoint progression should we use between levels, and how much overlap is reasonable?

nearMiss.query: Design the commission plan and quota for our account executives next year.
Write the level expectations for our engineering career ladder from junior to principal.
Draft an offer letter for a senior designer at 140,000 with a start date next month.

holdout.query: Our compensation structure is two years old. Age the market data, rebuild the pay ranges, and flag red-circle employees.

scenarios.task: Hypothetical facts: we have job levels L2, L3, L4 in one engineering family. Survey 50th percentile values effective 1 January are 85,000, 100,000, and 115,000. Our common effective date is 1 July. We have not chosen an aging rate. Employees: A at L3 earns 90,000, B at L3 earns 76,000, C at L4 earns 140,000. Build the bands with a 50% spread, compute compa-ratio and range penetration, and tell us the cost to bring people to minimum.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline invents an aging rate and an industry benchmark, confuses compa-ratio with range penetration, and suggests cutting the pay of the employee above maximum.
